<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Update python-google-nest-sdm to 7.0.0. This contains breaking API changes that use the async Google Cloud Pub/Sub APIs and move away from background threads. The APIs have been updated to make registration a little simpler, and internals require different approach to mocking. The tests have been updated to use simpler more generic fixtures based on `AiohttpClientMocker`, made with the minimal number of changes to existing tests.

This is meant to address #130407 as a side effect by simplifying all the network code, and being more resilient to failures with a simpler subscriber loop and retry handling that does not involve any threads.  The error handling was manually tested with breaking the network and observing everything can backoff nicely, then reconnect and resume.

Release Notes: https://github.com/allenporter/python-google-nest-sdm/releases/tag/7.0.0
Changes: https://github.com/allenporter/python-google-nest-sdm/compare/6.1.5...7.0.0

issue_context.title: Google Nest Integration loses connection with Nest Thermostats...
issue_context.body:
### The problem

For the last few days, I have noticed that my HA instance loses connection with the Nest Thermostat integration -- in that:

1. The `climate` sensor no longer responds to changes in the thermostat set points and vice-versa, I can't see changes on my dashboard
2. The corresponding temperature sensor doesn't record changes

Note that the thermostats are online in that I can reach them via the Google Nest app.
Also, I can manually read the thermostats using a shell script that does a `GET` request on the Google API so it's not a problem with the thermostats themselves or with my Google API credentials.

Reloading the integration (or restarting HA) seems to resolve the problem until it again loses connection... but this of course is not a solution...

The integration has been stable until now.

NOTE: it's possible that this was triggered by my thermostats going offline when I shut down my furnaces for cleaning and that somehow they then lost signal and were not re-discovered when I powered them back up....

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.11.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

core-2024.10

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Google Nest

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

### Diagnostics information

[config_entry-nest-9684e6c203aeccdb66cfc51d022534f8.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17711633/config_entry-nest-9684e6c203aeccdb66cfc51d022534f8.json)


### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
This is now happening multiple times a day -- unrelated to whether or not the system(s) are switched on/off.
Only solution is to reload the integration now multiple times a day every time I see it is out of sync.

Again manually using a shell script to ping the Google API doesn't have this issue so I don't think it's the Google API.
Similarly, since reloading fixes the problem temporarily, I don't think it's an issue with my authentication tokens.

Something definitely broke. Have there been recent changes to the Nest integration code that could have broken this?

Hey there @allenporter, could you please advise on this as you seem to be listed as  [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L980) for? Thanks!

Given that someone else subsequently posted a similar bug report, it would seem that this is not unique to me and the issue is severe given that it makes the Nest thermostat integration all but useless unless one writes a script to regularly reload it...

Thanks!

I am having this same issue.  Reintegration of Nest into Home Assistant did not fix the issue for me.  Creating a new topic while doing it did not fix the issue for me.  Creating a new cloud project did not fix it either.

The issue looks very similar to this old bug report that was closed out in the Spring, which seems like it had to be fixed on Google's end.
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/110010

FWIW, I just upgraded HA to 2024.11.2 and my thermostats are working again (and the setup flow works correctly again, too.)

I can't tell for sure whether that was @allenporter's bugfix or a Nest service issue that has since been fixed. Since both the setup flow issue and the thermostat state not updating are related to pub/sub, I suspect it may be the former?

> FWIW, I just upgraded HA to 2024.11.2 and my thermostats are working again (and the setup flow works correctly again, too.)
> 

2024.11.2 seemed to fix it for me as well.  I did have to remove and readd the Nest service to my Home Assistant, but that may be because I manually added during the outage, creating my own pub/sub.  The changes in 2024.11.2 have Home Assistant make its own now it seems.
Definitely don't create your own pubsub topic (yet) as it needs to match the one in the device access console.

[nest documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/nest)
[nest source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/tree/dev/homeassistant/components/nest)
This is the issue discussing the nest outage #130286 130532
Closing this issue, please reopen a new issue with the full issue template if you have any further issues, especially after 2024.11.2 which resolved some other problems. Thanks all.
@puterboy Either way:  the nest API is telling home assistant your thermostat is offline. This is not something home assistant can control.
So far stable with 2024.11.2

Happened again under 2024.11.2
Lost connection for more than a day until I noticed it... then resolved when I reloaded the Nest Integration.
@allenporter, I **do not** think this is due to Nest outage because my own non-HA test system I built to test MQTT messages continues to get them.

Please reopen this issue since bug still remains in 2024.11.2
Thanks!!!

Nest thermostats being reported as offline only happen when the nest server tells home assistant the thermostat is offline. There is not an integration bug here. There may be a nest server bug publishing incorrect messages and we'll need a lot of all messages received to report this to Google. (The nest integration queries the server on startup which papers I've the previously delivered offline message)

Well, it's happening to me about once a day -- and I am not alone.
What can I do to help debug?

(1) Enable debug logging and (2) capture nest sending you "offline" messages being published and never sending "online" messages. You can use this to file a report against google if you think it is a mistake for these messages to be published and your device i in fact online (or querying the API shows it online). If you see online messages published that home assistant is ignoring, then we can reopen the bug.

Hi, I am also experiencing this issue. It seems that updates on the status have not been processed correctly. In my example, the HVAC shows 'heating' for >15h until I manually reloaded the integration. The status is shown correctly on the Nest App itself. I cannot narrow it down to whether the status was not sent by Google or processed by Home Assistant. But from my perspective, it is still an ongoing issue and is not solved by updating to 2024.11.3.
See https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/130407#issuecomment-2509461613

I too have experienced this issue, but only on 2024.11+ Home Assistant releases. Every time I have tried updating to any of the 2024.11 HA releases, this issue crops up within 24 hours; all of a sudden, the Nest app in Home Assistant stops showing any status updates at all, and as such my automations depending on those status changes (heat turned on/off for example) never trigger.

I am always able to resolve the issue by rolling back to the 2024.10.4 HA release. On this release, the issue never occurs, and everything functions properly.

OK - I can reproduce the problem now 100% reliably.
The problem seems to occur when my router reboots (Note: the IP address is unchanged)
After rebooting, the Google Nest integration loses connection and needs to be restarted.

This really seems to be a HA/Nest integration problem since Google surely doesn't know that my router resets and presumably will continue to push changes as before...

See https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/130407#issuecomment-2509461613 on the information needed.

(The changes don't exactly get pushed directly like that. Home Assistant pulls them using a google pub/sub subscriber)

OK...
So I looked in both the debug logs for the Google Nest Integration... as well as wrote a short python that pulls messages from the Google Cloud Pub/Sub.
In both cases, after rebooting my router (with same WAN IP), the pub-sub messages stop.
So, the problem seems to be that during the reboot time, connection to the Google PubSub Cloud is lost and not regained.

Below is an excerpt from the Google Nest Integration log.
Everything is fine until about 15:38:18 when the Router is rebooted...
Then several google cloud services fail and in particular Google Nest subscriber is disconnected and shuts down.
The watchdog sees it shutting down and says it will restart in 10 seconds.
But it seems to fail to restart properly.
Finally at 15:42:39, I manually reload the integration and it starts receiving published messages again.

So it seems that either the watchdog is not restarting properly at all... or it tries but then gives up before the Router finishes rebooting and regains an Internet connection.

I believe that this is an HA/Nest integration issue since it is the client's duty to restart & resubscribe, not Google Cloud.

Again, I believe this had worked before, so perhaps something changed in the watchdog code, logic, or timing.

Hope this helps...

This is actually a more common/serious bug than I realized.
Not just rebooting the router but even changing settings on the router that causes a momentary loss in router connection causes the integration to exit.

Thanks @puterboy .  This describes exactly what I am experiencing, which had me baffled before reading this thread.  Based on your investigation I have now scheduled a reload of the Nest integration post router reboot, which seems to work, until a solution is available.

> Thanks @puterboy . This describes exactly what I am experiencing, which had me baffled before reading this thread. Based on your investigation I have now scheduled a reload of the Nest integration post router reboot, which seems to work, until a solution is available.

How are you scheduling a reload?

I know I can do it from cron using the REST API:

```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <LONG-LIVED-ACCESS-TOKEN>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" http://homeassistant:8123/api/config/config_entries/entry/<ENTRY-ID>/reload
```

Where:
`<LONG-LIVED-ACCESS-TOKEN>` can be generated from `http://<home-assistant>:8123/profile/security`
`<ENTRY-ID>` is the `entry_id` corresponding to `nest` in `core.config_entries` which can be obtained by:
```
jq -r '.data.entries[] | select(.domain == "nest") | .entry_id' /homeassistant/.storage/core.config_entries
```
It's possible using the automation UI. I simply trigger this at a specific time after router reboot.
Anything I can do to help fix this?
Just adding a comment as another user experiencing this same issue.
Thanks everyone for the detailed reports, I think we have all the information needed to understand the problem.

The integration needs to be resilient to recover on its own without any hacks or manual action on the part of the user.  No, I won't suggest any other workarounds.

I'm not yet able to reproduce the issue myself.  When I turn off my network adapter it handles everything just fine.

 I'm having a look at some of the internals to simplify them anyway essentially rewriting the entire network stack to be fully async and more resilient to problems, since some of the code for handling restarts is a little more complex than it needs to be and can use more modern apis provided in the cloud pubsub library.

Hello, you can read more about Home Assistant releases here: https://www.home-assistant.io/faq/release/ 

This fix will be in release 2025.2.0+. (It did not make it into the next upcoming release 2025.1.0 which will be released within the next week or so).
